summaries.body:
The 5.0.0 mapping records V3.4.1 as MODIFIED, moved from 4.0.3 V14.4.5, which required a Strict-Transport-Security header on all responses and for all subdomains, with the example max-age=15724800; includeSubdomains. The current clause still requires HSTS on all responses, sets a minimum max-age of one year, and requires the policy to apply to all subdomains at L2 and up.

Commits on predecessor ID V14.4.5 include elar's 25 April 2020 header-naming corrections (#720) and tghosth's May 2020 V14-Config.md updates. Commits stamped V3.4.1 (abhay's 11 February 2019 session CWEs, C6 tags) are the old cookie Secure occupant of that number. Mapping and the V14.4.5 predecessor text are the reliable origin.

Compared with 4.0.3 V14.4.5, the 5.0 text replaces the 15724800-second example with a one-year minimum max-age and makes include-subdomains a level split (L2 and up) rather than a universal requirement. elar's #720 header-naming pass and tghosth's V14-Config.md edits (including 055eb243 adding a modified tag on 8 April 2021) are the last attested 4.0-era events on that HSTS predecessor.

Issue #478 (divide V14.4 into disclosures, response headers, and request-header validation) is chapter structure around the predecessor, not a rewrite of max-age. Session-management commits on the V3.4.1 slot did not rewrite this HSTS control.
